title: Guest reviews — what gets published on your page
body:
Your guests can write a review on your page using a form: their name, one to five stars and a few sentences.
**Nothing is published without your decision** — a review does not appear on the page until you
decide about it.

![Screenshot: the review screen on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## Deciding from the email — no sign-in needed

You receive an email about every new review. The email has two buttons: „Publish to the page” and
„Don't publish”. You don't need to sign in: the button opens a confirmation page with the review text, and
there you decide with the **„Yes, publish it”** or the **„Yes, don't publish it”** button. Until you press
it, nothing changes — so your email program's link checker can't decide for you either.

The buttons in the email decide once: if you later change your mind, you can do so here, on the review screen
(see below).

## The review screen

On the Modules tab you reach it with the **„Setting”** link next to the review module. On the
**„Guest reviews”** card you see every review that has arrived, sorted into three groups — with
those still awaiting your decision at the front. Next to each group title you also see how many reviews it contains:

- **„Awaiting decision”** — you haven't decided about it yet, it doesn't appear on the page.
- **„On the page”** — it is published, visitors can read it.
- **„Not published”** — you decided not to publish it.

For each review you see the guest's name, the month and room the guest provided (if provided), the
stars and the text. Next to the stars the rating is also shown as a number (for example „4/5”), so
a bad rating catches your eye right away even if you don't look at the stars closely; the number of a
rating with 2 or fewer stars is shown in reddish. From a long review the first three lines are shown — you can
open it in full with the **„Full text”** link.

The buttons always offer what you can still do with that particular review:

- **„Publish”** — publishes it on the page (even if you didn't publish it earlier).
- **„Don't publish”** — for a review awaiting decision: it won't be published.
- **„Remove”** — removes an already published review from your page. The page is yours: you can
  take back a published review at any time.

After your decision, a line at the top of the card tells you what you did, and with whose review (for example
„Nagy Péter véleményét levette az oldaláról.”). The change appears immediately on your page too.

If no review has arrived yet, the card says so, and also that as soon as one arrives, you'll receive an email about it.

## What does the guest receive?

If you publish the review and the guest provided their email address, they receive a thank-you letter telling them that their
review is now visible on your page. A guest receives this letter at most once: if you
later remove and then publish the review again, no new thank-you letter is sent. If you don't publish it, the
guest receives no notification.

## Google rating

If your accommodation can be found on Google Maps and its details are clearly yours, the
**„Google rating”** card shows your Google average and the number of ratings. With the
**„See what people say on Google”** button you can look at the reviews themselves.

The card also tells you whether this number is currently showing on your page. If, further down among the **„Rules”**, you
turned off the **„Google review stars on the page”** switch, the card indicates this, and the
**„Go to toggle”** link takes you straight there.

The **text** of Google reviews cannot be copied onto your page because of Google's terms — we can only show the
average and the count, and a visitor who clicks is taken to the Google reviews. If the
Google data is unclear or old, we prefer not to show a number rather than possibly displaying another
accommodation's.

## Rules

At the bottom of the screen, on the **„Rules”** card, you can set how the module works — these rarely
need changing:

- **„Guests can leave reviews on the site”** — when turned off, the form disappears from your page; already
  published reviews remain.
- **„How many reviews to display”** — at most this many of the most recent published reviews are shown
  (1–20).
- **„Google review stars on the page”** — this decides whether the Google average also shows on your page.
  When turned off, the number is removed from your page.
- **„Also invite the guest who wrote the review to leave a Google rating”** — when turned on, in the thank-you letter
  we also ask the guest to write a few words on Google too. This is only sent to someone who has already
  stayed with you and already written to you — a Google rating improves how findable you are on the map.
- **„Notification address”** — this is where we send new reviews. Left empty, they go to the address linked to
  your sign-in.

You can save your changes with the **„Save settings”** button.
